slides.texte_overlay:
Things that make you surprisingly
good at texting her
Reply like a normal person. No waiting three hours on purpose, no games. If you're free and you want to answer, answer. Playing it cool usually just looks like you don't care, so stop doing it.
Send a photo instead of "wyd." The weird dog you just saw, the terrible menu at lunch. "This made me think of you." A small real moment beats another boring "how was your day" every single time.
Ask one question at a time. Not five in one message like a job interview. One good question, then actually react to her answer before you move on to the next thing you want to ask.

Make plans in text, talk in person. "Coffee on Saturday? I know a spot." Long texting marathons kill the mystery. Get to the date, and save the good stories for when you're actually sitting across from her.
Have something to bring to the conversation. Five minutes a day of history, art or science gives you endless openers. "Did you know otters have a favorite rock?" She'll actually want to reply.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: "hey" and "wyd" every night. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app, and you've got real things to share. "Did you know otters have a favorite rock?"

slides.texte_overlay: Don't send paragraphs after a short reply. If she answers with two words, she might be busy. Match her energy, keep it light, and pick it up later. Pressure through a screen is never attractive.
End the chat on a high note. Don't drag it on until it dies. "Alright, I'll let you go, talk tomorrow." Leaving while it's fun makes her look forward to the next message instead of dreading it.
